title: surface
content_html:
surface

Surface history and the layers and scarring in moments in an unfinished painting suggest that what meets the eye all at once can hold evidence of actions spread over years. A layer of paint, a sheet of glass and skin each let some things through and hold others back. How much of what we call depth is available through the surface, and what do we imagine from the marks it carries? Surface history Work · moments in an unfinished painting

Reading note. Buddhism. In the Pheṇa Sutta, a mirage is an image for examining perception. The apparent depth of a painted or photographic surface can also change as we come closer. What were we reading at a distance, and what does the surface give us to read now? Pheṇa Sutta, SN 22.95
